Unmatched rows, stacking and comparing data cuts

Source: vignettes/articles/derived-cards.Rmd
derived-cards.Rmd

A check on the canvas gives you counts. A derived card gives you the rows behind them, as a card of its own, with code that rebuilds it. Everything below uses small synthetic tables built in the page (no real patients).

Rows behind a count

A join check or a SUPP check offers buttons that open the rows behind its counts: the rows of either table with no match, the rows a date rule dropped, and the SUPP rows with no parent row or with an IDVARVAL that does not convert. The card is named for what it holds (ae_unmatched_dm) and is built by R from the tables as loaded, so a duckdb or Arrow input stays lazy. From the console, sv_unmatched() and sv_supp_orphans() return the same rows.

dm <- data.frame(USUBJID = c("S-01", "S-02", "S-03"), AGE = c(34, 51, 62))
ae <- data.frame(USUBJID = c("S-01", "S-02", "S-09"), AESEQ = 1L,
                 AETERM = c("Headache", "Nausea", "Rash"))
sv_unmatched(ae, dm, by = "USUBJID")
#>   USUBJID AESEQ AETERM
#> 1    S-09     1   Rash
sideview(dm, ae)   # connect USUBJID to USUBJID, then use the buttons on the join check

Stacking tables

sv_stack_check() lines up the columns of 2 to 8 tables and reports, per column, its type in each table and what a stack would do: the same type, a cast to a common type, a name that differs only by case offered as a rename, and a column missing from some tables. Nothing changes until you pick a fix. sv_stack() stacks the tables with the check’s fixes, adds a source column naming each row’s table, and turns a value that cannot be cast into NA.

wave1 <- data.frame(ID = 1:2, AGE = c(40L, 52L))
wave2 <- data.frame(ID = 3:4, Age = c(61, 47))
chk <- sv_stack_check(wave1 = wave1, wave2 = wave2)
sv_stack(wave1 = wave1, wave2 = wave2, check = chk)
#>   source ID AGE Age
#> 1  wave1  1  40  NA
#> 2  wave1  2  52  NA
#> 3  wave2  3  NA  61
#> 4  wave2  4  NA  47

In the gadget, the drawer has a Stack tab: pick tables, Check, change a fix, and Open adds the stacked table as a card.

Comparing data cuts

sv_compare(old, new, by) matches the rows of two cuts of a table on a key and counts the rows added (key only in new), removed (key only in old) and changed (key in both, a value differs). It also lists columns that were added, removed or changed type, and the changed values by column. Nothing is modified.

ae_old <- data.frame(USUBJID = c("S-01", "S-02", "S-03", "S-04"), AESEQ = 1L,
                     AETERM = c("Headache", "Nausea", "Rash", "Cough"),
                     AESEV = c("MILD", "MODERATE", "MILD", "SEVERE"),
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
ae_new <- data.frame(USUBJID = c("S-01", "S-02", "S-04", "S-05"), AESEQ = 1L,
                     AETERM = c("Headache", "Nausea", "Cough", "Dizziness"),
                     AESEV = c("MILD", "SEVERE", "SEVERE", "MILD"),
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
sv_compare(ae_old, ae_new, by = c("USUBJID", "AESEQ"))
#> ae_old -> ae_new, key USUBJID + AESEQ
#> Rows:    4 -> 4   added 1 · removed 1 · changed 1 · same 2
#> Columns: added none · removed none · type changed none
#> Changed values by column:  AESEV 1
#> added: 1 row
#> removed: 1 row
#> changed: 1 row

Here S-05 is new, S-03 is gone, and S-02 changed severity. In the gadget, the drawer’s Compare tab does the same: pick the old and the new table, Check, change the key if the suggestion is wrong (with no key picked, a CDISC tag suggests one), and Open each set of rows as a card: ae_new_added, ae_old_removed and ae_new_changed (the changed rows carry the old and new value side by side). Each card is one derive step whose R code is plain dplyr, and a duckdb or Arrow input stays lazy.

sideview(ae_old, ae_new)   # open the drawer, choose the Compare tab

The widget has no R, so it has no Compare tab; a saved compare step stays in the code, with a notice that the table is not shown.
